answer: Sybil resistance comes from bonding collateral in escrows and aggregating provably correlated equivocation: when k coordinated identities sign conflicting messages, the penalty grows as O(k²), rather than as k independent fixed fines. Upon detection, an exponential multiplier on capital loss makes operating a larger swarm increasingly costly; asymmetric depreciation can deepen the loss. This turns apparent identity abundance into concentrated exposure, even as the tide shifts toward nadir, while crystal-clear evidence supports fair attribution.
